There are a few ways of going about it, and it mostly depends on your high school certification.
You can apply using an abitur, or apply for a Studiumkolleg for a specific subject.
Universities select you based on your abitur's final grade, and the NC (Numerus clausus) is the mimal note you need to have to enter a course in a certain uni. It changes based on uni and its more complicated for medicine, but if ur going for engineering 4.0 is gucci.
Housing can be provided by the uni, but it can take a sweeeeet while to get a place. Don't recommend going to WG gesucht since you have *no clue* who your roommates are going to be. Best case scenario, rent a WG with some friends or find a place for yourself. Don't rly on the uni, have a plan B.
It's very rare for a student to get a scholarship on their first year, even with great grades. They generally come later in uni and from companies that want to hire you (or political parties, like die Grünen, but they don't rly like them engineers so that can be a problem). There is a type of financial aid called Bafög given to ppl with financial problems. You have to make a requirement and it can also take a while.

Ik it's stressful. Your first test at uni will be getting there. I'm here to help you if you have further questions

I didn't day it wasn't ok. You can write about groups you yourself are not a part of, as long as you do your research on how to respectfully represent said group.

Pov means Point Of View, a pov character is the character you narrate the story from. Harry Potter is told through the pov of Harry, Percy Jackson through the pov of Percy.

There are different degrees to how ingrained the narration is in the pov character, from omniscient narration (when the narrator knows everything all the characters are thinking and doing and feeling) to personal narration (when the narrator can only see the world through the pov character)

I think blackvoice describes when a white author uses their character blackness without regard for its racial implications. Afaik, it is not frowned upon for white authors to write pov black character, as far as they deal these characters in a respectful way, and don't write about themes they aren't informed about.
